- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 7-day high), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.3) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.1–0.3), model shows mean-reversion bias; shift forecast toward recent 7-day average, not 30d trend.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% gap), and sentiment is positive, consider “lag correction” — delay forecast peak by 1–2 days to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize “sell-off exhaustion”; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent days if sentiment turns negative.
